messages.subject: nimble cannot estimate Probit model
parts:
I am a fresher in nimble, but in my recent practice, i found that nimble cannot estimate probit model correctly, I cannot figure out where the problem is. please point out my fault or give me some advice. Thanks for all of your advice.
Here is my code


#### generating fake data
sim_probit = function(N,beta){
library(nimble);
set.seed(1)
X = matrix(rnorm(N*length(beta),0,1),N,length(beta))
Y = X%*%beta
Y = Y+rnorm(N,0,0.75)     
for (i in 1:N) Y[i] = ifelse(pnorm(Y[i])>runif(1),1,0)
return(list(Y=Y,X=X,N=N))
}
data = sim_probit(N = 100,beta = c(0.5,0.6))

##nimble code for my model
spp_code <- nimbleCode({
for (i in 1:K){
beta[i] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
}
epsilon ~ dnorm(0,1)
y_star[1:N] <- x[1:N,1:K]%*%beta[1:K]+epsilon
for (j in 1:N){
y[j] ~ dbern(phi(y_star[j]))
}
})

spp_Model <- nimbleModel(code=spp_code,constants=list(N = data$N,K=ncol(data$X)),
data=list(y = as.numeric(data$Y),x = apply(data$X,2,scale) ),#winbugs examples suggest scaling data_X 
inits=list(epsilon=0,beta=rep(0,ncol(data$X)))
)

spp_md = nimbleMCMC(spp_Model,summary = TRUE,niter=5000, nburnin=100)

#### results
####            mean     sd   t_val
#### beta[1] -0.6423 0.1652 -3.8875
#### beta[2]  0.8101 0.1796  4.5114
#### epsilon -0.1653 0.1447 -1.1427

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: nimble cannot estimate Probit model
parts:
Hello, thanks for the query.  The fundamental problem going on is the fact that your model only estimates one single "epsilon" term, which is used for every single observation in y.  This is in contrast to your data-generation, which has a separate "error term" for each observation, on the line:

Y = Y+rnorm(N,0,0.75) 

where you add a different normally-distributed error to each row of Y.

This can be fixed by changing your model code.  You could either have N different epsilon terms:

spp_code <- nimbleCode({
    for (i in 1:K){
        beta[i] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
    }

epsilon[j] ~ dnorm(0,1)
        y[j] ~ dbern(phi(y_star[j] + epsilon[j]))
    }
})

Or, you could embed the error using a normal distribution.  This is mathematically equivalent to the code above:

spp_code <- nimbleCode({
    for (i in 1:K){
        beta[i] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
    }

y_p[j] ~ dnorm(y_star[j], 1)
        y[j] ~ dbern(phi(y_p[j]))
    }
})

In either case, you'll have to make some changes to your initial values list, since in the first case, epsilon is no longer a scalar, and in the second case, epsilon doesn't even exist (although you might provide initial values for the y_p terms).

Give this a go, and it should accurately estimate the model.  You may also consider a slightly longer burn-in period than 100 iterations, maybe perhaps 500 or 1000.

Cheers,
Daniel
